title: From command to code audit
summary: Follow a scan from the command line to instruction discovery, rule matching, scoring and a JSON report.

steps.label: Command
steps.title: Start with one command
steps.explanation: A path and output flag enter the scan parser. The path defaults to the current directory; --json selects machine-readable output. The scan entry point rejects a path that is not a directory before loading any policy.
steps.insight: The command chooses the output format. It does not change how findings are detected.
steps.transition: The validated directory becomes the policy lookup root.

references.quote:
def build_scan_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-config-score", description="Score and audit coding-agent instruction files.")
    p.add_argument("path", nargs="?", default=".", help="Repository path (default: current directory)")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Print JSON instead of text")
    p.add_argument("--html", metavar="FILE", help="Write a self-contained HTML report")
    p.add_argument("--badge", metavar="FILE", help="Write an SVG score badge")
    p.add_argument("--sarif", metavar="FILE", help="Write a SARIF 2.1.0 report for GitHub code scanning")
    p.add_argument("--fail-under", type=int, default=None, metavar="N", help="Override the repository policy score floor")
    return p

steps.label: Policy
steps.title: Load the repository policy
steps.explanation: load_policy looks for .agentconfigscore.json under the repository root. If it is absent, a default Policy is returned. If it is present, the file is parsed and validated. Configuration errors stop the command with exit code 2.
steps.insight: The --fail-under CLI flag can override the policy floor. The configured suppressions are passed into analysis.
steps.transition: analyze receives the root and the policy suppressions.

steps.label: Discover
steps.title: Find the instruction files
steps.explanation: Discovery walks the repository, ignores excluded paths, and keeps supported instruction files. It recognizes AGENTS.md and other known names, plus Markdown rules in supported tool directories. Results are sorted by relative path.
steps.insight: This is a targeted instruction audit: it does not scan every source file as an instruction.
steps.transition: Only the selected instruction files enter the reading loop.

steps.label: Read
steps.title: Turn files into analysis context
steps.explanation: Each discovered file is read as UTF-8 with replacement for decoding errors. The scanner stores its text, builds instruction context and estimates its token size. A read error becomes a finding; an empty instruction file gets its own error.
steps.insight: The token count is an estimate, not a tokenizer measurement or a runtime model cost.

steps.transition: The original text and its context feed deterministic checks.

steps.label: Match rules
steps.title: Match a rule, keep its source location
steps.explanation: Pattern rules search the text. Some command rules parse options; dangerous-command matches are skipped when the surrounding context prohibits the command. An accepted match becomes a finding with the rule ID, relative file path and line number.
steps.insight: A match is a deterministic review signal. It does not prove that a command ran or that an instruction is malicious.
steps.transition: After other repository checks and suppression handling, active findings reach scoring.

references.quote: Rule("sudo", "warning", "danger", 6, "Privileged command in persistent agent instructions", "Flags instructions that encourage an agent to execute commands with elevated privileges."),

steps.label: Score
steps.title: Apply penalties within category caps
steps.explanation: The scanner groups penalties by category and applies only the remaining capacity in each cap. It subtracts the applied penalties from 100. If any active finding is an error, the score is capped at 89; then the score determines the grade.
steps.insight: For the simplified one-warning illustration, 100 − 6 = 94 (A). This is arithmetic for an example, not a measured result for a repository.

input.label: Active findings · example
input.value:
one sudo warning
penalty = 6; danger cap = 35

steps.transition: The Report bundles score, grade, findings and suppression audit data.

references.quote:
used = Counter()
    penalty = 0
    for finding in findings:
        rule = RULES_BY_CODE.get(finding.code)
        category = rule.category if rule is not None else "other"
        cap = CATEGORY_CAPS.get(category, CATEGORY_CAPS["other"])
        applied = min(finding.penalty, max(0, cap - used[category]))
        used[category] += applied
        penalty += applied

    score = max(0, 100 - penalty)
    if any(finding.severity == "error" for finding in findings):
        score = min(score, 89)
    grade = "A" if score >= 90 else "B" if score >= 80 else "C" if score >= 70 else "D" if score >= 60 else "F"
    order = {"error": 0, "warning": 1, "info": 2}
    return Report(
        root=str(root), files=rels, score=score, grade=grade,
        estimated_tokens=total_tokens, duplicate_ratio=duplicate_ratio,
        findings=sorted(findings, key=lambda f: (order.get(f.severity, 3), f.file, f.line or 0)),

steps.label: Report
steps.title: Choose an output, then return an exit code
steps.explanation: The same Report is serialized to JSON or printed for people. Optional HTML, badge and SARIF files are written earlier in this function. After output, the command returns 1 when the score is below the selected floor, otherwise 0.
steps.insight: A finding does not by itself make a normal scan return 1. This scan path uses the score floor; regression commands have their own gate.
steps.transition: End of the scan path. Follow another feature from the tour library.

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "root": self.root,
            "files": self.files,
            "score": self.score,
            "grade": self.grade,
            "estimated_tokens": self.estimated_tokens,
            "duplicate_ratio": round(self.duplicate_ratio, 4),
            "findings": [f.to_dict() for f in self.findings],
            "suppressed_findings": [item.to_dict() for item in self.suppressed_findings],
        }
